faqs.a: WPM (words per minute) = (correct characters ÷ 5) ÷ minutes. The '5' is the standard word length used by typing tests worldwide. Only correct characters count, so accuracy directly affects your score.

30–40 WPM is average for casual typists, 50–60 is solid for office work, and 80+ is genuinely fast. Professional transcriptionists often exceed 100 WPM. Consistency matters more than peak speed — steady, accurate typing beats bursts with errors.
faqs.q: What is a good typing speed?

typing-test.formula:
WPM = (correct characters ÷ 5) ÷ minutes elapsed
Accuracy = (keystrokes − errors) ÷ keystrokes × 100
Backspace deletes the last character but the error already counted stays counted.

typing-test.workedExample:
60-second test, 300 correct characters, 315 keystrokes, 15 errors:
1. WPM = (300 ÷ 5) ÷ 1 = 60 WPM.
2. Accuracy = (315 − 15) ÷ 315 × 100 = 95.2%.
3. Verdict: solid office speed with good accuracy — push for 65 WPM next.
